subject: general
question: During the British rule in India, about how much per cent of the country's population lived mostly in villages and derived their livelihood directly or indirectly from agriculture?
solution:
The correct answer is__ "***85%***".__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India's economy remained mostly agricultural during the British colonial era because ***85%*** of the country's people lived in villages and depended on agriculture for their livelihood.
 
• Almost half of India's national GDP came from*** *****agriculture** and related sectors.
 
• Nevertheless, while employing such a sizable population, the agricultural sector continued to develop and occasionally face extraordinary **decline**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Although the total area under cultivation*** *****increased**, agricultural productivity decreased even if the sector saw a considerable gain in absolute terms.
 
• The different land settlement schemes that the colonial authority implemented were mostly to blame for the stagnation in the **agricultural sector**.
 
• Particularly, under the **zamindari system**, which was put in place in the former **Bengal Presidency**, which included some of the modern-day eastern states of India, the profit generated by the agricultural sector went to the zamindars rather than the cultivators.
 
• However, a sizable portion of zamindars—not simply the colonial administration—did nothing to improve the*** *****state of agriculture**.
